title: Terraform Drift
summary: Terraform drift is the divergence between the infrastructure state recorded in a Terraform state file and the actual configuration of the resources deployed in a cloud account, arising when something changes a resource outside the pipeline that created it. The change might be a console fix during an incident, a script in a legacy automation path, a provider-side default that shifted, an imported resource never brought under management, or an attacker deliberately relaxing a control such as a firewall rule or bucket policy. Drift matters because the infrastructure-as-code repository stops being a trustworthy description of reality: a plan run after drift will silently revert the out-of-band change, reviews of pull requests no longer describe the live environment, and a security control that appears present in code may have been removed in production. Detection normally relies on scheduled plans or a refresh-only plan that reports differences without applying them, remote state with locking to prevent concurrent writes, and consistent provider versions so that cosmetic differences do not obscure real ones. Handling drift requires judgement rather than blind application, because some drift is legitimate emergency remediation that should be codified back into the repository, while unreviewed drift in security-relevant attributes is an incident indicator. Mature teams track drift as a metric, alert on changes to sensitive attributes, and reconcile by importing or amending code rather than by overwriting production.
objectives: You will be able to explain how state, configuration files and live resources can diverge and why that breaks review assumptions.
You will be able to interpret a refresh-only plan and separate meaningful drift from cosmetic provider differences.
You will be able to triage unreviewed changes to security-relevant attributes as potential malicious activity.
You will be able to reconcile drift by importing or amending code instead of overwriting production state.
You will be able to describe how remote state, locking and pinned provider versions reduce false drift signals.
You will be able to design a drift detection cadence and reporting path for a platform team.

beginner.definition: Terraform is a tool that builds cloud infrastructure from written files. Drift is the gap between what those files say and what is really running. It appears when somebody changes a resource by hand, through a web console or a script, instead of through the usual pipeline that created it.
beginner.whyItMatters: When drift exists, your written files no longer describe reality. A reviewer approves a safe change, but production may already differ. A firewall rule that looks closed in code may be open in the live account. Worse, an attacker who quietly weakens a control creates drift on purpose. Finding drift turns a silent change into something you can see and question.
howItWorks: Terraform keeps a state file that records what it believes it created.
On a schedule, you run a check that reads the real cloud resources again.
The check compares the real settings with the recorded state and your written files.
Differences are listed as a plain report, and nothing is changed yet.
Your team decides what each difference means: a quick fix, an old script, or an attack.
Safe changes are written into the files, and unwanted ones are reversed.
beginner.example: Imagine a shared kitchen with a written recipe pinned to the wall. One evening someone swaps the salt for sugar to save time and forgets to update the recipe. The next cook follows the pinned recipe and is confused by the result. Drift is that stale recipe: the kitchen and the instructions no longer match.
takeaways: Drift means your written files no longer match the live environment.
Check for drift on a schedule and treat security settings as high priority.
Reconcile by updating the files or importing resources, not by guessing.

exercises.title: Terraform Drift - EASY
exercises.summary: Recall and recognition: definitions, one clear answer, single-step questions.

exercises.title: Terraform Drift - MEDIUM
exercises.summary: Application: read a short log or alert and choose the correct next step.

exercises.title: Terraform Drift - HARD
exercises.summary: Analysis: a multi-step scenario with distractors, evidence to weigh, and a reason to give.

exercises.title: Terraform Drift - EXTREMELY HARD
exercises.summary: Synthesis under pressure: incomplete evidence, competing priorities, and a decision you must defend.
